description: Mediterranean island (various polities 500–1861) whose Giudicati (judges) constituted the only indigenous governance between Byzantine, Arab, Pisan, Genoese, and Aragonese competition; the four Giudicati, Cagliari, Torres, Arborea, and Gallura, maintained a distinctive legal culture and Sardinian language while the island's grain resources attracted Italian merchant competition; Aragonese conquest (1324) established Iberian dominance that shaped Sardinian society into the modern era.

temporal.notes: Stub: dates from GeoJSON basemap years 1000–1400

lifecycle_phases.description: Sardinia was a Byzantine province but difficult to govern; local Sardinian Giudicati emerged as de facto rulers.
Four Sardinian judiciaries (Cagliari, Torres, Arborea, Gallura) governed the island with local autonomy.
Giudicato of Arborea led resistance against Aragonese invasion; Eleonora of Arborea issued famous law code.
Aragonese conquest completed after decades of warfare; Sardinia became a Crown of Aragon possession.

rise_factors.description: Island geography allowed the development of unique Sardinian institutions independent of mainland powers.
Eleonora of Arborea's military and legal leadership (Carta de Logu, 1395) symbolised Sardinian resistance.

decline_factors.description: Aragonese naval and land power ultimately overwhelmed Sardinian resistance after sustained campaigns.
